basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Dixit iterum Deus ad Abraham: Et tu ergo custodies pactum meum, et semen tuum post te in'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Dixit iterum Deus ad Abraham: Et tu ergo custodies pactum meum, et semen tuum post te in generationibus suis; hoc est pactum quod observabitis inter me et vos et semen tuum post te: Circumcidetur ex vobis omne masculinum; et circumcidetis carnem praeputii vestri, ut sit in signum foederis inter me et vos. Benigna provisione Dominus primo pactum gratiae suae statuit beato Abrahae et semini ejus; ac deinde ab illis pactum obedientiae requirit: ut minus videlicet terreat labor certaminis, audito prius praemio perpetuae remunerationis. Circumcidi ergo praecipitur caro praeputii, in signum foederis inter Deum et homines, ut hoc signo admonerentur fideles illius temporis, mundandos se ab omni inquinamento carnis et spiritus, perficiendam sanctificationem in timore Dei; sed et altiore mysterio fiebat circumcisio illa carnalis in signum foederis inter Deum et semen Abrahae, quia nimirum in illius foederis signum data est, de quo supra dictum est eidem Abrahae: Atque in te benedicentur universae cognationes terrae; quod ad gratiam novi testamenti pertinere nemo fidelium dubitat. In hujus ergo foederis signum nemo fidelium dubitat, quod circumcisus est Abraham et semen ejus in carne praeputii sui, ut praefiguraretur typice nasciturus de illius semine, qui electos suos ab omni macula peccatorum expurgaret, ac perpetua benedictione donaret; cujus expurgationis sacramento congruit apte quod sequitur:
